title: Nike's Original Air Max Is the Latest Sneaker to Get a Limited-edition Oregon Ducks Release
text:
The University of Oregon's Ducks of a Feather NIL brand is releasing a limited-edition Nike Air Max 1 exclusively at Flight Club Tokyo. Find out more.
1 takes a more subtle approach with its Tokyo-exclusive colorway. Shifting from the all-green look of the aforementioned ’22 iteration, the upcoming DOAF x“Tokyo” has been draped in a gray-based colorway which, according to a press release, is inspired by the Japanese capital’s philosophy of simplicity and craftsmanship.
All About Ben Stiller's Custom 'Good Luck Kicks' He Wears Courtside to the Knicks Playoffs Games -- and the Second Finals-themed Pair on the WayThe otherwise toned-down color palette is energized by a vibrant multicolor Swoosh logo that’s said to reference the neon lights of Shibuya and Harajuku. The multicolor effect is also carried over to the tongue’s Duck head logo, a custom detail which has previously only been seen on the aforementioned Hatfield-designed colorway.
At the heel, the multinational connection is further emphasized with embroidered Japanese characters that translate to “GO DUCKS. ” Football Showcase,which takes place from June 25 to June 27 and will include in-person drills from Ducks players teaching on-field skills, core concepts and techniques.
“The Tokyo Oregon Football Showcase continues our legacy of creating innovative programs for student-athletes that are unmatched in the industry,” Rosemary St. Clair, chief executive officer of Oregon’s Division Street NIL initiative, said in a press release. “This event will be a celebration of how sport transcends borders and creates lasting cultural connections.
Our goal is to introduce Oregon athletes and the Duck football brand to Japanese fans and establish a foundation of excitement and fan engagement that we can build on in future years. ”Tokyo is limited to only 300 pairs worldwide and will be released June 28 exclusively from Flight Club’s Tokyo location. Retail pricing is 28,000 Japanese yen, which converts to around $174 as of publishing.
The sneakers will be raffled with in-store and online drawings opening June 23 and closing June 26. And on the final day of the drawing, Hatfield himself will be in attendance for a meet-and-greet event, with more details to be announced soon on Flight Club’s Instagram.
